findings.title: Core task definition is still a forecasting task, not sponsorship
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROW 4 (unhighlighted text between two yellow runs)
findings.evidence: "Based on the information you receive, your task is to predict which candidate, A or B, will perform better on a separate logical reasoning test."
findings.why_it_matters: The 4/16 meeting concluded the paradigm was 'too focused on accuracy' and redefined Stage 2 as 'How strongly do you endorse your organizational candidate' (tab_4_16_meeting.txt lines 5, 24). This sentence, the participant's one-line job description, is verbatim old-paradigm prediction framing, is NOT yellow-highlighted (so it is stale pilot text that was never rewritten), and still uses 'A or B'. A coauthor reading only this row would conclude the study is still a forecasting experiment, which is exactly what the redesign exists to fix.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite as an advocacy task, e.g.: "Your task is to decide how strongly to endorse [ORGANIZATION 1: Vertex]'s candidate, the candidate you represent, when they are matched against a candidate from [ORGANIZATION 2: Beacon], based on their performance information." (Exact wording depends on resolving the free-choice vs must-endorse fork; see the contradiction finding.) Highlight the rewrite yellow.
findings.verdict_notes: Every element of the finding checks out against the source files. (1) The quoted sentence exists verbatim in tab_endorser.txt, TABLE ROW 4 (line 18): "Based on the information you receive, your task is to predict which candidate, A or B, will perform better on a separate logical reasoning test." (2) It is genuinely unhighlighted and sits exactly where claimed: the preceding text (lines 16-17) is inside [HL#ffff00] yellow runs ending with [/HL] immediately before the sentence, and the next yellow run opens at line 20 ("In each candidate set, the organization labels will indicate..."). (3) The claimed problem follows from the canonical brief: the 4/16 meeting notes contain "Are we too focused on accuracy?" (tab_4_16_meeting.txt line 5) and redefine Stage 2 as "How strongly do you endorse your organizational candidate" (line 24), and the design brief states the redesign exists because the old paradigm was "too much of a forecasting experiment." (4) "A or B" also conflicts with the canonical genderless ID-only + org-badge candidate presentation. The severity logic holds: this is the participant's one-sentence job description in the Stage 2 instructions, and per the yellow-highlight convention its unhighlighted status marks it as stale pilot text never rewritten, so it misleads a coauthor about the core task and directly implicates brief ask #4 (hedgy/contradictory advocacy framing) and ask #6 (stale unhighlighted text). The proposed fix correctly defers exact wording to the unresolved free-choice vs must-endorse fork, which the brief explicitly says not to silently resolve. Note the adjacent unhighlighted slider paragraph (line 19, "unsure which candidate will outperform the other") shares the same forecasting framing, which reinforces rather than undermines the finding.

findings.title: Free-choice vs must-endorse-own-candidate contradiction; tab contains ONLY the free-choice framing
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROWS 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 vs 4/16 Meeting tab
findings.evidence: Free-choice side (every passage): ROW 4 "predict which candidate, A or B, will perform better" and "unsure which candidate will outperform the other"; ROW 5 "which candidate you favored"; ROW 6 "whether the candidate you favored (indicated by your slider position) actually performs better" and "if you endorsed the wrong candidate"; ROW 7 option "You endorse the wrong candidate"; ROW 8 "predict which candidate is more likely to excel"; ROW 10 "What is the objective when choosing who to recommend?", "use the slider to honestly indicate which candidate you believe will perform better", and yellow: "Some candidate sets may require you to decide whether to endorse the candidate from [ORGANIZATION 1: Vertex], the organization you represent, or the candidate from [ORGANIZATION 2: Beacon], another organization." Must-endorse side: ZERO passages in this tab; it exists only in 4/16 meeting notes ("How strongly do you endorse your organizational candidate") which themselves also contain the other fork ("Make a decision between own organization versus other organization").
findings.why_it_matters: The May 30 fork (must endorse own candidate and rate only strength, vs slider can favor the rival) is unresolved, and the Endorser tab silently resolves it one way: pure free choice. That collides with the June 2 Evaluator-tab comment directing that evaluators be told they only ever see own-org endorsements; if sponsors can freely favor the rival, that Stage 3 claim becomes untruthful (IRB flag 1). Also internally wrong: ROW 10's "Some candidate sets may require" contradicts ROWS 4 and 8, which state EVERY set is one own-org vs one rival-org candidate, so 'Some ... may' is false under either fork.
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the fork explicitly at the next lab meeting, then make the tab univocal. If must-endorse: rewrite ROWS 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 around 'how strongly do you back your organization's candidate'. If free choice: delete 'Some ... may require' (it is every set), and reconcile the Evaluator tab / June 2 comment. Do not field until one framing is chosen.
findings.verdict_notes: All quoted evidence exists verbatim at the claimed locations. tab_endorser.txt rows 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 10 contain only the free-choice framing (slider can favor either candidate, "endorse the wrong candidate" is possible), and the full tab contains zero must-endorse-own-candidate language; that framing appears only in tab_4_16_meeting.txt ("How strongly do you endorse your organizational candidate", line 24), which also carries the rival fork ("Make a decision between own organization versus other organization", line 16). The June 2 2026 comment (doc_comments.txt id AAAB8qTe4lg) exists exactly as described and is anchored to Evaluator-tab text saying evaluators see "whether the candidate they endorsed was from the endorser's own organization or from another organization", so the truthfulness/IRB collision follows. The internal ROW 10 contradiction also holds: ROWS 4 and 8 state every candidate set is one own-org vs one rival-org candidate, making ROW 10's yellow "Some candidate sets may require" false under either fork. The design brief explicitly instructs auditors to flag this unresolved fork rather than silently pick one, and IRB flag 1 supports critical severity. Only trivial imprecision: the ROW 6 quote is truncated (continues "on the logical reasoning task than the other candidate"), which does not affect the claim.

findings.title: Earnings row: unfinished third bonus factor stub contradicts the stated two-factor scheme and leaves the Stage 3 telegraph undisclosed
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROW 6 (yellow stub at end of row)
findings.evidence: "Your earnings depend on two factors." ... "you can earn a bonus of up to $3 based on: (1) the accuracy of that endorsement decision and (2) how much the evaluator was willing to stake on that endorsement decision." followed by the yellow stub: "Three: likelihood that your organization's candidate wins [fix writing]"
findings.why_it_matters: The row simultaneously tells participants the bonus has two factors and drafts a third, with an explicit [fix writing] placeholder in what is participant-facing table text. Worse, the canonical design requires the Stage 3 social-capital DVs ('do you want to keep seeing candidates from this organization/sponsor') to truthfully telegraph into the sponsor's bonus, so per the May 30 IRB flag Stage 2 MUST disclose that component, and it appears nowhere. There is also an unaddressed incentive-compatibility tension: factor three rewards favoring your own org's candidate while ROW 10 instructs sponsors to "honestly indicate which candidate you believe will perform better" and factor one rewards accuracy. This blocks fielding.
findings.proposed_fix: Finish the third factor as real participant-facing text (e.g., "Third, part of your bonus depends on the evaluator's decisions about your organization: after seeing your endorsements, the evaluator allocates future review slots to your organization and to you; each slot allocated adds $X to your bonus"), change "two factors" to "three", state the payment rule for each factor with dollar amounts, and reconcile the honesty instruction with the own-org incentive.
findings.verdict_notes: All three quotes exist verbatim in Endorser tab TABLE ROW 6 (the "two factors" framing, the (1)/(2) bonus list, and the yellow-highlighted stub "Three: likelihood that your organization's candidate wins [fix writing]"), and the honesty instruction is in ROW 10 as claimed. The canonical brief's hard flag #1 requires Stage 2 to disclose ALL bonus components because the Stage 3 social-capital DVs must truthfully telegraph into sponsor pay; no such component appears anywhere in the Endorser tab (rows 5-6 disclose only accuracy and evaluator stake), so the undisclosed-telegraph claim, the two-vs-three contradiction, the participant-facing placeholder, and the accuracy-vs-own-org incentive tension all hold. Critical severity is justified (IRB truthfulness / unfinished participant-facing text blocks fielding).

findings.title: Ownership/affiliation of the own-org candidate is hedged and circular, never stated as sponsorship
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROW 4 (final yellow run); absence throughout ROWS 4-10
findings.evidence: "Because you are assigned to represent [ORGANIZATION 1: Vertex], your endorsement may be interpreted as an endorsement made by a [ORGANIZATION 1: Vertex] endorser."
findings.why_it_matters: "may be interpreted as" is maximally hedged, and the clause is circular: an endorsement by a Vertex endorser says nothing about advocating FOR Vertex's own candidate. The canonical redesign requires the endorsement to read as "advocacy for one's own person" (sponsor-protege relationship). Nowhere in the tab does language like "your candidate", "your organization's candidate", or any stake in that candidate's success appear outside the ROW 6 stub. Since org affiliation IS the redesign's core manipulation, communicating it this weakly risks the study not manipulating what it claims to manipulate.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with unhedged ownership language, e.g.: "You represent [ORGANIZATION 1: Vertex]. The [ORGANIZATION 1: Vertex] candidate in each set is YOUR organization's candidate. Your endorsement will be shown to evaluators as [ORGANIZATION 1: Vertex] backing its own candidate, and part of your bonus depends on how your organization's candidates fare." Repeat the ownership frame in ROWS 5, 8, and 10.
findings.verdict_notes: Evidence verified verbatim in tab_endorser.txt ROW 4 final yellow run (line 20): "your endorsement may be interpreted as an endorsement made by a [ORGANIZATION 1: Vertex] endorser" — hedged and circular as claimed. Absence claim also verified: ROWS 4, 5, 8, 10 use only neutral "the organization you represent" affiliation language; the sole ownership/stake language is the unfinished ROW 6 stub "Three: likelihood that your organization's candidate wins [fix writing]". This directly fails canonical requirement that the endorsement "reads as advocacy for one's own person" and matches audit ask #4 (ownership hedging), so critical severity is justified for the core manipulation. Caveat on the proposed fix only: it must not silently resolve the unresolved forced-vs-free endorsement fork (ROW 10 still allows endorsing the Beacon candidate), which the brief says to flag, not pick.

findings.title: Forecasting/prediction framing pervades ROWS 8, 9, and 10, all unhighlighted stale pilot text
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROWS 8, 9, 10 (unhighlighted portions)
findings.evidence: ROW 8: "Your endorsement represents your prediction for candidates' performance on the logical reasoning task." and "use the available performance information to predict which candidate is more likely to excel at the logical reasoning task." ROW 9: "Understanding these tasks will help you make better predictions about candidates' logical reasoning performance." ROW 10: "use the slider to honestly indicate which candidate you believe will perform better on the logical reasoning task"
findings.why_it_matters: Beyond the ROW 4 task definition, the prediction vocabulary saturates the instructions, so the yellow org-affiliation additions read as a bolt-on to an unchanged forecasting study rather than a sponsorship study. Per the doc's own convention, text that must change should be re-written and highlighted; none of these sentences are.
findings.proposed_fix: Sweep 'predict/prediction' out of ROWS 8-10 and recast as endorsement strength: e.g. ROW 8 "Your endorsement represents how strongly you back your organization's candidate to outperform the rival organization's candidate on the logical reasoning task." Highlight all rewrites yellow.
findings.verdict_notes: All four quotes verified verbatim and unhighlighted in tab_endorser.txt (ROW 8 line 42, ROW 9 line 46, ROW 10 line 53); only the org-affiliation insertions in those rows carry [HL#ffff00]. The claim follows from the brief: the redesign exists precisely because the old paradigm was "too much of a forecasting experiment," and the doc convention (yellow = changed) plus audit asks #4/#6 make pervasive unhighlighted predict/prediction language a real framing+highlighting defect. Severity "important" is apt. Caveat on the remedy only: the proposed rewrite ("how strongly you back your organization's candidate") silently resolves the brief's flagged unresolved fork (must-endorse-own vs. slider-allows-rival); ROW 10's own highlighted text takes the rival-allowed reading, so the sweep should be fork-neutral or deferred to that fork's resolution. This does not alter the finding itself.

findings.title: Earnings row opens with two near-duplicate sentences describing different splits
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROW 6, first two sentences
findings.evidence: "Your earnings depend on two factors. Your earnings from this session are composed of two parts. No matter what, you will receive $1 for completion..."
findings.why_it_matters: Two consecutive redundant openers, and they describe different decompositions: 'two factors' refers to the bonus formula (accuracy x evaluator stake) while 'two parts' refers to flat fee + bonus. A participant cannot tell which 'two' is which, and both become wrong once the third bonus factor lands. There is also a missing space mid-row ("...that endorsement decision.First, the size of your bonus...").
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the first sentence and restructure: "Your earnings have two parts: a guaranteed $1 completion fee and a bonus of up to $3. Your bonus depends on three factors: (1)... (2)... (3)..." Fix the 'decision.First' spacing.
findings.verdict_notes: Verbatim quote exists exactly as claimed at tab_endorser.txt line 27, Endorser tab TABLE ROW 6, opening sentences: "Your earnings depend on two factors. Your earnings from this session are composed of two parts. No matter what, you will receive $1 for completion of this part of the study." The two openers do describe different decompositions: the same row later says "you can earn a bonus of up to $3 based on: (1) the accuracy of that endorsement decision and (2) how much the evaluator was willing to stake" (the 'two factors' reading) while 'two parts' maps to $1 flat fee + bonus. The missing space is also real and verbatim: "...how much the evaluator was willing to stake on that endorsement decision.First, the size of your bonus depends partially on..." The problem follows from the canonical brief: the row ends with the yellow-highlighted third-factor stub "Three: likelihood that your organization's candidate wins [fix writing]", so both the 'two factors' framing and the enumerated (1)/(2) list become false once the drafted third bonus component lands, and the brief mandates full disclosure of all bonus components (telegraph truthfulness / IRB flag 1). Severity 'important' is appropriate: participant-facing pay instructions that are internally redundant and soon-to-be inaccurate, fixable before fielding.

findings.title: Comprehension question matches only the two-factor bonus rules and breaks once factor three is added
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROW 7
findings.evidence: "Which scenario results in a positive bonus for you?" with keyed answer "You endorse the correct candidate with the slider away from 50; the evaluator bets 40%." and distractor "You endorse the correct candidate; the evaluator bets 0%."
findings.why_it_matters: As written today the key is uniquely correct under ROW 6's two-factor rules (slider at 50 = no bonus; wrong candidate = no bonus; 0% bet = $0). But under the drafted third factor ("likelihood that your organization's candidate wins") or the social-capital telegraph, the 0%-bet distractor could still pay a positive bonus, making two options defensible and the screen-out unfair. The CQ also tests nothing about the org-affiliation structure, the redesign's core element.
findings.proposed_fix: After ROW 6 is finalized, rewrite the CQ so every distractor is unambiguously zero under ALL bonus components, and add one CQ item verifying participants know which organization they represent and that one candidate per set is their own organization's.
findings.verdict_notes: Evidence verified verbatim in tab_endorser.txt: ROW 7 (lines 33-38) has the exact CQ, keyed answer, and 0%-bet distractor quoted; ROW 6 (lines 27-29) has the two-factor bonus rules plus the yellow-highlighted third-factor stub "Three: likelihood that your organization's candidate wins [fix writing]". The problem follows from the canonical brief: with a drafted org-win bonus component (and the brief's statement that Stage 3 social-capital allocations truthfully telegraph into the sponsor's bonus), the "correct candidate; evaluator bets 0%" distractor could pay a positive bonus, making two answers defensible; if anything the finding understates it, since the slider-at-50 and wrong-candidate distractors could also pay whenever the org's candidate wins. ROW 7 is the only earnings CQ on the tab and no item tests org-affiliation comprehension, so the secondary claim also holds. Severity "important" is appropriate given ROW 6 is explicitly unfinished.

findings.title: 'Stake'/'bet' terminology and evaluator mechanic contradict the canonical Stage 3 wager design; random-selection payment rule underspecified
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROW 5 (yellow-adjacent text) and TABLE ROW 6
findings.evidence: ROW 5: "they will decide what percentage of their own bonus (0–100%) to stake on your endorsement being correct." ROW 6: "evaluators' bets will be a number between 0 to 100 representing how much of their own earnings they are willing to stake on your endorsement" and "Your bonus earnings are based on one of your endorsements, selected at random."
findings.why_it_matters: Canonical terminology is 'wager' and '$0.50 bank', NEVER 'stake'; Stage 2 describes the evaluator's decision as staking a percentage of 'their own bonus/earnings', which misdescribes the actual per-round $0.50-bank wager mechanic. Also, in Stage 3 one evaluator makes THREE wagers on the same sponsor and multiple evaluators may see the same endorsement; which wager pays the sponsor is unspecified, and the IRB truthfulness flag requires this description of downstream consequences to be accurate.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace 'stake'/'bet' with 'wager', describe the evaluator mechanic accurately ("the evaluator wagers 0-100% of a $0.50 bank on your endorsement"), and specify the selection rule (e.g., "one endorsement and one evaluator wager on it will be selected at random for payment").
findings.verdict_notes: All three quotes exist verbatim at the claimed locations (tab_endorser.txt ROW 5 line 24; ROW 6 lines 27-28). The 'stake'/'bet' terminology and 'percentage of their own bonus/earnings' description contradict the canonical Stage 3 mechanic ('wager 0-100% of a $0.50 bank per decision', terminology NEVER 'stake'). The random-selection payment rule is genuinely underspecified: with one evaluator making three wagers per sponsor and multiple evaluators per sponsor (N~100 sponsors vs ~600 evaluators), ROW 6 never states which evaluator's wager pays, and the brief's hard flag 1 (telegraph truthfulness / IRB) makes that accuracy mandatory. The same 'bet' language also recurs unflagged in ROWs 7 and 10, reinforcing the finding. Severity 'important' is appropriate.

findings.title: Slider description is position-anchored, not org-anchored, and the proposed mockup anchors own org on the LEFT against the own-org-right decision
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROW 4 (unhighlighted slider paragraph) and ROW 12 proposed image [IMAGE:kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz]
findings.evidence: ROW 4: "moving the slider toward 0 indicates you favor the candidate on the left, moving it toward 100 indicates you favor the candidate on the right". The proposed mockup's slider poles read "Vertex candidate" (left, own org) and "Beacon candidate" (right); the ROW 10 prototype image and current mockups still read "A will perform better" / "B will perform better".
findings.why_it_matters: The May 30 panel decision was to relabel the poles by ORG with own org anchored on the RIGHT (preserving |v-50|*2 strength math). The verbal instructions were never updated from generic left/right language, the one org-labeled mockup puts own org on the wrong side, and the ROW 10 prototype still shows old A/B poles. Left/right language also implies candidate side varies, which contradicts a fixed org anchor.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite ROW 4: "The slider ranges from 0 to 100. Your organization's candidate is always on the right: moving toward 100 means you more strongly endorse your organization's candidate; moving toward 0 means you favor the other organization's candidate; 50 means you favor neither." Regenerate the mockup with [ORGANIZATION 1] on the right pole.
findings.verdict_notes: ROW 4 quote verified verbatim and unhighlighted (tab_endorser.txt line 19): "moving the slider toward 0 indicates you favor the candidate on the left, moving it toward 100 indicates you favor the candidate on the right" — still position-anchored, never updated to org poles. The ROW 12 proposed mockup (kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz, images/Endorser__mxo6oc7vxrwz.png) shows "Vertex candidate" on the LEFT pole (0) and "Beacon candidate" on the RIGHT (100); Vertex is the own org ([ORGANIZATION 1: Vertex]), so the only org-labeled mockup anchors own org opposite the canonical May 30 decision ("own org anchored on the right"). The ROW 10 prototype image (kix.s36nf4j6pu3j) confirmed to still read "A will perform better" / "B will perform better". All three evidence claims exist where stated and the contradiction with the canonical brief follows. Severity 'important' is appropriate (fieldable only after fix; misleads coauthors about the anchoring/strength-math convention).

findings.title: Mockups show gendered candidate avatars; canonical design requires genderless ID-only candidates
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROWS 12-15 images, including the proposed mockup [IMAGE:kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz]
findings.evidence: Proposed mockup shows a woman silhouette avatar over "Candidate A / ID aoygoszl / Vertex" and a man silhouette over "Candidate B / ID 49ki2ruu / Beacon"; current mockups (kix.3lqsjv2poktq, kix.hl94nhui7wu5) likewise pair woman/man silhouettes.
findings.why_it_matters: Canonical design: "Candidates are GENDERLESS (ID-only, no name/avatar) so the only gender cue in the study is the endorser." If Stage 2 stimuli carry candidate gender, sponsors' endorsements become confounded with candidate gender, contaminating the endorsement stimuli that Stage 3 evaluators react to and undermining the claim that endorser gender is the study's only gender cue.
findings.proposed_fix: Regenerate all Stage 2 mockups with no avatars: ID + org badge + percentile cards only.
findings.verdict_notes: Verified against images/Endorser__mxo6oc7vxrwz.png, Endorser__3lqsjv2poktq.png, Endorser__hl94nhui7wu5.png: candidate cards carry clearly gendered silhouette avatars (proposed row-12 mockup: woman over "Candidate A / ID aoygoszl / Vertex", man over "Candidate B / ID 49ki2ruu / Beacon"), directly contradicting the canonical brief's "Candidates are GENDERLESS (ID-only, no name/avatar) so the only gender cue in the study is the endorser." No doc comment or tab text handles removing candidate avatars. All four proposed mockups (rows 12-15) are byte-identical (156962 bytes) per images_manifest.json, so the defect spans the whole mockup set. Only trivial imprecision: in the two "current" mockups the order is man (A) / woman (B), not woman/man, which does not affect the claim. Severity "important" is appropriate: these are labeled prototype mockups, so fixable pre-fielding, but if fielded as-is the candidate-gender confound would contaminate both Stage 2 endorsements and the Stage 3 stimuli built from them.

findings.title: Stale 'Candidate A/B' labels in text and all mockups
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROW 4 and images in ROWS 10, 12-15
findings.evidence: ROW 4: "predict which candidate, A or B, will perform better"; mockups display "Candidate A" / "Candidate B" card titles and "A will perform better" / "B will perform better" slider poles even alongside org badges.
findings.why_it_matters: A/B naming is the old paradigm's neutral-forecast furniture. With org affiliation as the identity that matters, A/B labels compete with and dilute the org labels, and keep the left/right-varies mental model alive.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop A/B everywhere; refer to candidates by org ("the [ORGANIZATION 1: Vertex] candidate") plus ID in stimuli.
findings.verdict_notes: Core claim holds: A/B naming persists in text and mockups. ROW 4 quote is verbatim (tab_endorser.txt line 18: "your task is to predict which candidate, A or B, will perform better on a separate logical reasoning test"), and the "Proposed:" org-badged mockups in ROWS 12-15 (Endorser__mxo6oc7vxrwz / tyugwp2r16u / scntbjdij0e4 / h65pj8a0h5jn — all the identical duplicated placeholder the brief warns about) do show "Candidate A" / "Candidate B" card titles directly above the Vertex/Beacon org badges. However, the evidence overclaims on the slider poles: in the proposed org-badged mockups the slider poles are ALREADY org-labeled ("Vertex candidate" on the left, "Beacon candidate" on the right), not A/B. The "A will perform better" / "B will perform better" poles appear only in (a) the ROW 10 standalone slider image (Endorser__s36nf4j6pu3j), which has no org badges, and (b) the "current" reference images (e.g. Endorser__3lqsjv2poktq), where old labels are expected per the doc's current-vs-proposed convention. So the "even alongside org badges" claim is true for card titles but false for slider poles. Severity 'minor' and the proposed fix stand. (Side note outside this finding's scope: those org-labeled poles put the own-org Vertex candidate on the LEFT/0 end, contradicting the brief's "own org anchored on the right".)
findings.corrected: Corrected evidence: Endorser tab ROW 4 (line 18): "predict which candidate, A or B, will perform better"; proposed mockups in ROWS 12-15 show "Candidate A"/"Candidate B" card titles alongside Vertex/Beacon badges, but their slider poles already read "Vertex candidate"/"Beacon candidate". A/B slider-pole labels appear only in the ROW 10 slider-only image (no org badges) and in the "current" (old-paradigm) reference images.

findings.title: All four 'Proposed:' mockup images are one byte-identical duplicate that does not depict its row's scenario
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROWS 12-15 (images kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz, kix.tyugwp2r16u, kix.scntbjdij0e4, kix.h65pj8a0h5jn)
findings.evidence: MD5 of all four proposed images: e47a03d25127732a1370238514029263 (identical). The single image shows slider at 50 with Vertex 75th/1st vs Beacon 17th/78th, so rows labeled "[A dominant]" and "[B slightly better]" display an uncertain-choice mockup.
findings.why_it_matters: The brief notes duplicated placeholders were suspected; this confirms all four are the same file. Coauthors reviewing the [A dominant] and [B slightly better] rows are looking at the wrong stimulus, so scenario-specific design choices (e.g., how a dominant profile pairs with org affiliation) have never actually been mocked up.
findings.proposed_fix: Render three additional distinct proposed mockups matching the [A dominant], second [Uncertain choice], and [B slightly better] profiles and replace the duplicates.
findings.verdict_notes: All claims verified against source files. (1) Duplication: md5sum of the four proposed images (images/Endorser__mxo6oc7vxrwz.png, __tyugwp2r16u.png, __scntbjdij0e4.png, __h65pj8a0h5jn.png) returns e47a03d25127732a1370238514029263 for all four, and images_manifest.json shows identical byte size 156962 for all four. (2) Locations: tab_endorser.txt confirms the images sit after "Proposed:" in TABLE ROW 12 "[Uncertain choice]" (kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz), ROW 13 "[A dominant]" (kix.tyugwp2r16u), ROW 14 "[Uncertain choice]" (kix.scntbjdij0e4), ROW 15 "[B slightly better]" (kix.h65pj8a0h5jn). (3) Content: opening the image shows the slider at 50 with caption "50 — I have no idea which candidate will perform better", Candidate A (Vertex badge) 75th/1st percentile vs Candidate B (Beacon badge) 17th/78th — a mixed, genuinely uncertain profile matching only the [Uncertain choice] rows, so rows 13 ([A dominant]) and 15 ([B slightly better]) display a mockup that does not depict their scenario. The brief explicitly says "several are known to be duplicated placeholders", so this finding confirms and quantifies a suspected issue; severity 'minor' is appropriate.

findings.title: Both org badges in the proposed mockup use the same yellow color; canonical assigns distinct off-gender-palette colors per org
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROW 12 proposed image [IMAGE:kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz]
findings.evidence: The "Vertex" and "Beacon" badge pills are both rendered as identical yellow/amber pills; canonical spec: "Atlas violet #7C3AED, Vertex amber #B45309, Beacon teal #0F766E".
findings.why_it_matters: Same-colored badges remove the at-a-glance visual discrimination of which candidate is own-org vs rival-org, weakening the affiliation salience the redesign depends on, and the final stimuli must keep org colors off the pink/blue gender palette.
findings.proposed_fix: Recolor badges per the canonical palette (Vertex amber #B45309, Beacon teal #0F766E) in all regenerated mockups.
findings.verdict_notes: Evidence verified. tab_endorser.txt TABLE ROW 12 contains "Proposed:" followed by [IMAGE:kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz] (images/Endorser__mxo6oc7vxrwz.png). Opening the PNG shows the "Vertex" badge (Candidate A) and "Beacon" badge (Candidate B) rendered as visually identical yellow/amber pills. The canonical brief explicitly assigns distinct per-org colors off the gender palette: "Atlas violet #7C3AED, Vertex amber #B45309, Beacon teal #0F766E" (design_context.md, Focal manipulation section). Beacon should be teal #0F766E, not the same yellow as Vertex, so same-colored badges do defeat at-a-glance own-org vs rival-org discrimination. Severity 'minor' is reasonable since this is a proposed mockup, not fielded stimuli, and yellow at least stays off the pink/blue gender palette. (Note, outside this finding's scope: the same mockup also shows gendered candidate avatars, which contradicts the genderless-candidates spec — a separate, more serious issue.)

findings.title: Em dash in participant-facing mockup caption plus run-on typos in tab text

findings.title: Entire Stage 3 payout and flow is written for TWO decisions, not the canonical THREE rounds

findings.evidence: ROW 8: "Today you will evaluate two decisions made by the same endorser.For each decision, you start with a bank of $0.50." ... ROW 10: "Today you will evaluate one endorser and their two decisions. Click the arrow to begin." 4/16 Meeting: "Repeated rounds (3 rounds)".
findings.why_it_matters: The redesign's within-subject backbone is R1 -> outcome -> R2 -> outcome -> R3 -> outcome with a new candidate pair each round; the primary model includes a round term. Every count-bearing sentence in the NEW table, plus a comprehension check that screens people out, encodes the old two-decision pilot. The dollar math is internally consistent for two decisions ($1.00 max x 2 = $2.00) but wrong for three ($3.00 max), so a coauthor cannot tell whether three rounds was dropped or never written in.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite ROW 8 as: "Today you will evaluate three decisions made by the same endorser, each involving a new pair of candidates. For each decision, you start with a bank of $0.50..." (also fixes the missing space in "endorser.For"); change the bonus line to "the sum of all three decisions (up to $3.00 maximum)"; ROW 10 to "one endorser and their three decisions"; CQ5 correct answer to "The sum of all three decisions"; add a mockup row for the third round.
findings.verdict_notes: All quoted evidence exists verbatim at the claimed locations (Evaluator tab NEW table ROW 8 lines 38/45, ROW 9 CQ5 lines 72-75, ROW 10 line 79; 4/16 Meeting line 30 "Repeated rounds (3 rounds)"). The canonical brief mandates three rounds with a round term in the primary model, and a full scan of the NEW table (rows 1-13, including all yellow-highlighted additions) shows no mention of three rounds anywhere — every count-bearing sentence plus the screen-out comprehension check encodes the old two-decision design, and the $2.00 max is consistent only with two decisions. Severity 'critical' is warranted: fielding as written would run the wrong design and CQ5 would screen participants against the wrong answer. Sole nit: the proposed fix's 'add a mockup row for the third round' is unverified — rows 11-13 are unlabeled image mockup rows, so relabeling vs adding is undetermined; this does not affect the finding itself.

findings.title: June 2 comment not implemented: instructions still tell evaluators they may see own-org OR other-org endorsements
findings.location: Evaluator tab, NEW table, ROW 6 (final yellow-highlighted paragraph, the exact text the unresolved comment anchors to) and ROW 6 first highlighted sentence; also ROW 7
findings.evidence: ROW 6: "You will also see whether the candidate they endorsed was from the endorser’s own organization or from another organization. In other words, you will know the extent to which the endorser placed their endorsement behind their own organization’s candidate." Comment (2026-06-02, unresolved): "update to make sure that it only communicates that evaluators see their own organization's candidates". Also ROW 6: "Each endorser made endorsement decisions involving candidates from their own organization and candidates from another organization." ROW 7: "their candidate does indeed perform better/worse than the randomly chosen alternate participant".
findings.why_it_matters: The design shows evaluators ONLY endorsements of the endorser's own-org candidate; "whether ... own organization or from another organization" and "the extent to which" promise variation that never occurs, which is both deceptive (IRB) and dilutes the affiliation manipulation the redesign exists to create. ROW 7's "better/worse" hedge similarly implies the endorsement direction can vary, mirroring the unresolved Stage 2 forced-endorsement fork; the June 2 comment mandates the own-org-only reading for this tab regardless.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the ROW 6 final paragraph with own-org-only language, e.g. "For each endorsement, you will see the organization the endorser was assigned to represent. The candidate they endorsed is always from the endorser's own organization, and the comparison candidate is from another organization." Rewrite ROW 6 sentence 1 as "Each endorsement decision involved one candidate from the endorser's own organization and one candidate from another organization." In ROW 7 change "perform better/worse than the randomly chosen alternate participant" to "performs better than the other organization's candidate". Then resolve the comment.
findings.verdict_notes: All three quoted passages exist verbatim where claimed: ROW 6 final yellow-highlighted paragraph (tab_evaluator.txt line 30, NEW table) is exactly the quotedFileContent of unresolved comment AAAB8qTe4lg dated 2026-06-02T13:58:39Z with content "update to make sure that it only communicates that evaluators see their own organization's candidates"; ROW 6 sentence 1 is at line 27; ROW 7 "perform better/worse than the randomly chosen alternate participant" is at line 35. The problem follows from the canonical brief (design_context.md ask #5 and hard flag #1: telegraph truthfulness/IRB): evaluators only ever see own-org endorsements, so promising "whether ... own organization or from another organization" is untrue and dilutes the affiliation manipulation. Critical severity is warranted. One caveat that does not change the verdict: ROW 6 sentence 1 ("decisions involving candidates from their own organization and candidates from another organization") is technically reconcilable with the canonical own-org-vs-rival pair structure and is ambiguous rather than flatly false; the finding's proposed disambiguating rewrite handles this correctly.

findings.title: Comparison standard contradicts itself: 'other organization' in instructions vs 'randomly selected candidate from the remaining pool' in the comprehension check
findings.location: Evaluator tab, NEW table, ROW 6, ROW 7, ROW 9 (CQ2)
findings.evidence: ROW 6: "how confident they were that a given candidate from their own organization would score higher on the logical-reasoning test than another randomly selected candidate from the other organization." ROW 7: "the randomly chosen alternate participant". ROW 9 CQ2: "Who is the endorsed candidate compared against to determine whether the prediction was correct? •  A randomly selected candidate from the remaining pool (correct)".
findings.why_it_matters: Canonically each candidate set is one own-org candidate vs one specific rival-org candidate whose profile the endorser saw, so "randomly selected" misdescribes Stage 2 in all three passages. Worse, the graded-correct CQ2 answer omits the organization entirely and uses old-design "remaining pool" language, so an attentive participant who internalized ROW 6 finds no matching option, and the screen-out (must pass all) teaches or enforces the wrong mental model of the focal comparison.
findings.proposed_fix: Standardize on the paired rival: ROW 6 "...would score higher on the logical-reasoning test than the candidate from the other organization in the same set"; ROW 7 "the other organization's candidate"; CQ2 correct answer "The candidate from the other organization in the same candidate set", keeping "A randomly selected candidate" as a distractor if desired.
findings.verdict_notes: All three quotes verified verbatim at the claimed locations (tab_evaluator.txt NEW table: ROW 6 line 28, ROW 7 line 35, ROW 9 CQ2 lines 56-57 with "(correct)" marker). ROW 9 has no highlight runs, so CQ2 is stale unhighlighted old-design text while ROW 6's org framing is yellow-highlighted new text — the contradiction and the "must pass all" screen-out logic are real. Adjustment: the claim that "randomly selected" misdescribes Stage 2 "in all three passages" overreaches. The canonical brief says only "Each candidate set = one own-org candidate vs one rival-org candidate" and does not specify how the rival is chosen, so ROW 6/7's "randomly selected/chosen ... from the other organization" is compatible with the canonical design (random draw from the rival org's pool). The confirmed defect is CQ2 specifically: its graded-correct answer "A randomly selected candidate from the remaining pool" omits the organization entirely and reuses pre-redesign pool language, contradicting the updated ROW 6 instructions and teaching/enforcing the wrong comparison model via screen-out. Severity 'critical' remains defensible on CQ2 alone; the proposed fix to CQ2 stands, while the ROW 6/7 rewording is optional polish rather than a canonical-design violation.
findings.corrected: Core contradiction is between ROW 6 (yellow-highlighted "from the other organization") and ROW 9 CQ2 correct answer "A randomly selected candidate from the remaining pool (correct)" (tab_evaluator.txt lines 28 and 56-57). ROW 6/7's "randomly selected" phrasing is not itself contradicted by the canonical brief, which leaves the rival-selection mechanism unspecified.

findings.title: No comprehension check tests the org-affiliation structure
findings.location: Evaluator tab, NEW table, ROW 9 (all five CQs)
findings.evidence: The five CQs cover: "What task(s) must the endorsed candidate score higher on", "Who is the endorsed candidate compared against", "How much do you start with", "You wager 50%... What do you earn?", "How is your total bonus calculated?" None mentions organizations, the endorser's assignment, or that the endorsed candidate is from the endorser's own organization.

The focal affiliation manipulation is introduced in yellow-highlighted new text in ROW 6 ("assigned to represent an organization... whether the candidate they endorsed was from the endorser's own organization"), and ROW 4 frames the whole survey as a comprehension test of these instructions, so the absence of any affiliation CQ is a real gap. The sponsor-pay telegraph (ROW 7) is also untested by any CQ, consistent with the proposed fix.
