findings.title: No selection rule for which Stage 2 endorsements evaluators see; own-org vs rival endorsements uncontrolled
findings.location: Endorser tab TABLE ROW 5 and ROW 10; Evaluator tab (NEW) TABLE ROW 6; unresolved comments AAAB8qTe4lg (2026-06-02) and AAABtL3bCKM (2025-10-24)
findings.evidence: Endorser ROW 5: "a subset of your endorsements will be shown to an evaluator (another participant)". Endorser ROW 10 (yellow): "Some candidate sets may require you to decide whether to endorse the candidate from [ORGANIZATION 1: Vertex], the organization you represent, or the candidate from [ORGANIZATION 2: Beacon], another organization." Evaluator NEW ROW 6 (yellow): "You will also see whether the candidate they endorsed was from the endorser's own organization or from another organization." Unresolved comment: "update to make sure that it only communicates that evaluators see their own organization's candidates". Separate unresolved comment: "over sample on the extreme endorsers since we do expect women to be more penalized".
findings.why_it_matters: The doc is silent on how the shown subset is drawn. If sponsors can favor the rival (ROW 10 framing) but evaluators only ever see own-org endorsements (June 2 comment intent), the shown set is conditioned on sponsor behavior, truncating the strength distribution; if rival endorsements can be shown, endorsement direction becomes an uncontrolled moderator of the wager DV. Nothing states the endorsement stream is yoked/identical across Man/Woman arms, and the unexecuted 'oversample extreme endorsers' plan would add deliberate non-random sampling. Any of these can confound the endorser-gender effect on wagers.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a bracketed implementation note to Evaluator NEW ROW 6 stating the exact rule, e.g.: "[Evaluators always see endorsements of the endorser's OWN organization's candidate. The displayed endorsement stream (direction and strength) is scripted and identical across Man/Woman arms; endorser gender is randomly assigned independent of endorsement content.]" Resolve the Stage 2 forced-choice vs free-slider fork first, and delete or formalize the oversampling comment.
findings.verdict_notes: Every quoted piece of evidence exists verbatim where claimed: Endorser ROW 5 subset sentence (tab_endorser.txt line 24), Endorser ROW 10 yellow rival-choice framing (line 55), Evaluator NEW ROW 6 yellow own-org-or-other sentence (tab_evaluator.txt line 30), and both unresolved comments AAAB8qTe4lg (2026-06-02, anchored to that exact ROW 6 sentence) and AAABtL3bCKM (2025-10-24, oversampling) in doc_comments.txt. The NEW Evaluator table contains no selection rule for which endorsements are shown and no statement that the displayed stream is yoked/identical across Man/Woman arms; the canonical brief mandates identity across arms only for the outcome sequence, and its ask #5 targets precisely the June 2 comment. The confound logic (behavior-conditioned truncation if own-org-only from a free slider; uncontrolled direction moderator if rival endorsements shown; deliberate non-random sampling if the oversampling comment is executed) follows. Notably, the OLD/archive Evaluator table ROW 4 DID specify a rule ("randomly selected from the entire set of the endorser's decisions"), so the omission is a regression from the archived version, which strengthens rather than weakens the finding. Severity 'critical' is justified: it bears directly on the focal endorser-gender effect on the wager DV and would mislead a coauthor about how stimuli are generated.

findings.title: Comparison standard told to evaluators (random draw) contradicts the paired own-vs-rival design; CQ2 trains the wrong standard
findings.location: Evaluator tab (NEW) TABLE ROW 6, ROW 7, and ROW 9 (comprehension check 2); vs Endorser tab TABLE ROW 4
findings.evidence: Evaluator NEW ROW 6: "how confident they were that a given candidate from their own organization would score higher on the logical-reasoning test than another randomly selected candidate from the other organization." ROW 7: "their candidate does indeed perform better/worse than the randomly chosen alternate participant". ROW 9 CQ2: "Who is the endorsed candidate compared against...? A randomly selected candidate from the remaining pool (correct)". But Endorser ROW 4: "For each candidate set, you will be shown two candidates... your task is to predict which candidate, A or B, will perform better".
findings.why_it_matters: In Stage 2 the endorser compares two specific candidates whose performance profiles they saw; the win event is within that pair. Telling evaluators the benchmark is a random draw (and 'from the remaining pool' does not even mention the rival organization) misstates the objective win probability they should infer, injects uncontrolled variance into wagers, and the comprehension check screens people INTO the study only if they hold the wrong model. 'perform better/worse' is also incoherent as a payoff description.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite Evaluator ROW 6/7 to: "...would score higher on the logical-reasoning test than the other candidate in the same set, who was from the other organization." Fix ROW 7 to drop "/worse" and "randomly chosen alternate participant". Change CQ2 correct answer to "The other candidate in the same candidate set (from the other organization)".
findings.verdict_notes: All four quoted passages exist verbatim at the claimed locations (tab_evaluator.txt NEW ROW 6 line 28, ROW 7 line 35, ROW 9 CQ2 lines 56-57; tab_endorser.txt ROW 4 lines 17-18). The canonical brief defines candidate sets as one own-org vs one rival-org candidate with the win event inside the observed pair, and the evaluator tab's OLD ROW 4 confirms the within-pair standard ("scores higher... than the other candidate"). Telling evaluators the benchmark is "another randomly selected candidate" / "the remaining pool" misstates the comparison the endorser actually made (against a specific rival whose scores the endorser saw), and CQ2 screens participants IN only if they affirm that wrong model. ROW 7's "better/worse" is verbatim and incoherent. The highlight pattern shows ROW 6 was partially org-patched while the comparison-standard language and CQ2 were left stale, matching the brief's audit ask #6. Contextual nuance (not overturning): the "randomly selected candidate" wording is inherited from the fielded pilot's CQ5, so it is a stale carryover rather than a new invention, but under the redesign it contradicts the core paired own-vs-rival structure, so critical severity stands.

findings.title: Displayed endorsement strength not specified as equated/scripted across gender arms; jitter and display-range scheme absent
findings.location: Evaluator tab (NEW) TABLE ROWS 6-8 and ROWS 11-13 (mockups showing "82% — very confident"); unresolved comments AAAB2MnNcvI ("change the extremes (~10% vs 90%)") and AAAB2MnNcvA ("within the same tercile (but add a little bit of variance)")
findings.evidence: The NEW table never states how the displayed slider position/confidence is generated. The only strength content is in mockups: "Endorser's confidence ... 82% — very confident" (kix.is8axhdh3ngr / kix.vha7uuc4k2ve). The two March 19 comments specifying the 10-90 display extremes and within-tercile jitter remain unresolved and appear nowhere in the table text.
findings.why_it_matters: Endorsement strength is the strongest determinant of the wager. If displayed strength is not scripted identically (or yoked) across Man/Woman arms, any gender difference in wagers or wager deltas is confounded by strength. The canonical design mandates round-to-round jitter of +/-5-12 points clamped to the same tercile with q2_strength_delta as a control; none of this is in the doc, so an implementer reading only the doc would field an unequated design.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an implementation note to the NEW table (near ROW 8): "[Displayed strength: raw |v-50|*2 mapped to 10-90 display range; Round 1 strength identical across Man/Woman arms; later rounds display Round 1 strength +/- 5-12 points clamped to the same tercile; save endorser_display_strength per round and q2_strength_delta as a mandated control.]" Resolve the two March 19 comments into this note.
findings.verdict_notes: All evidence checks out. (1) The Evaluator NEW table (tab_evaluator.txt rows 1-13) contains zero specification of how the displayed endorsement strength is generated: no |v-50|*2 mapping, no 10-90 display range, no statement that Round 1 strength is scripted/equated across Man/Woman arms, and no round-to-round jitter rule. Grep for tercile/jitter/variance/display across all tab_*.txt returns nothing in the Evaluator tab; the only related text is the 3/19 meeting note ("maybe it makes sense to add a little bit of noise between decisions"), which is meeting commentary, not table spec. (2) The mockups do show a concrete strength with no provenance: both Evaluator__is8axhdh3ngr.png and Evaluator__vha7uuc4k2ve.png (rows 11) display "Endorser's confidence ... 82% — very confident" — verified by opening the PNGs. (3) Both cited comments exist verbatim and unresolved in doc_comments.txt: AAAB2MnNcvI ("change the extremes (~10% vs 90%)", 2026-03-19) and AAAB2MnNcvA ("within the same tercile (but add a little bit of variance)", 2026-03-19); neither is reflected anywhere in table text. (4) The canonical brief (design_context.md) mandates the +/-5-12 same-tercile jitter with q2_strength_delta as control and lists strength as a scripted factor of the 8-condition design, so an implementer reading only the doc would field an unequated design; strength confound of the gender effect on wagers follows directly. Severity 'critical' is justified. One trivial location imprecision: the mockups are only in rows 11-13, not rows 6-8; rows 6-8 are the instruction rows where the spec is absent — the finding's parenthetical reads correctly under that split, so no adjustment needed.

findings.title: Proposed Stage 2 mockup shows gendered candidate avatars, violating the genderless-candidate requirement
findings.location: Endorser tab TABLE ROWS 12-15, image kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz (byte-identical copies kix.tyugwp2r16u, kix.scntbjdij0e4, kix.h65pj8a0h5jn, all 156962 bytes); unresolved comment AAAB01xlE_s
findings.evidence: The "Proposed:" mockup renders Candidate A (Vertex, own org) with a woman-silhouette avatar and Candidate B (Beacon) with a man-silhouette avatar, above "Vertex candidate / Beacon candidate" slider labels. Erika's unresolved comment: "these are the old images, right? we're no longer referring to people as 'Candidate B'?" The same 156,962-byte image is pasted as the 'Proposed' for all four scenario rows ([Uncertain choice], [A dominant], [Uncertain choice], [B slightly better]).
findings.why_it_matters: The canonical design requires candidates to be GENDERLESS (ID-only, no name/avatar) so the ONLY gender cue in the study is the endorser. The proposed mockup leaks candidate gender into Stage 2 and couples it with org (woman = own-org side), which would contaminate both the sponsor's endorsement decisions and, if propagated, the evaluator-stage stimuli. The duplicated placeholder also means the four scenario rows do not actually show their labeled scenarios, so strength/scenario coverage cannot be checked.
findings.proposed_fix: Regenerate the four proposed Stage 2 mockups with ID-only candidate cards (no avatars, matching the Evaluator proposed mockup kix.vha7uuc4k2ve, which correctly shows the candidate as ID + org badge only), one distinct image per scenario row, and add a bracketed note: "[Candidates are displayed with ID and org badge only; no names, avatars, or gender cues.]"
findings.verdict_notes: All evidence verified: rows 12-15 of tab_endorser.txt each carry a "Proposed:" image (kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz, kix.tyugwp2r16u, kix.scntbjdij0e4, kix.h65pj8a0h5jn) and MD5 hashing proves all four are byte-identical (e47a03d25127732a1370238514029263, 156962 bytes each). The image shows Candidate A (Vertex, own org) with a woman-silhouette avatar and Candidate B (Beacon) with a man-silhouette avatar over "Vertex candidate / Beacon candidate" slider labels, violating the canonical requirement that candidates be genderless (ID-only, no name/avatar; endorser is the only gender cue) and coupling candidate gender with org. Unresolved comment AAAB01xlE_s (Erika Kirgios) exists verbatim. The proposed-fix reference to Evaluator kix.vha7uuc4k2ve is accurate (candidate shown as ID + org badge only, no avatar). Two immaterial caveats: the Erika comment is dated 2026-03-09 (pre-May-30) with no quoted anchor, so its attachment to these specific images is inferred not proven; and the design brief already flags that several proposed mockups are duplicated placeholders, so the duplication sub-claim is known context. The core gendered-avatar leak is real and severity 'critical' is justified.

findings.title: Sponsor bonus disclosure incomplete: third factor is an unfinished stub, social-capital telegraph channel undisclosed in both stages
findings.location: Endorser tab TABLE ROW 6 (yellow stub); Evaluator tab (NEW) TABLE ROW 7; 4/16 Meeting tab ("Binary items (telegraph this to the sponsor as a bonus)")
findings.evidence: Endorser ROW 6 opens "Your earnings depend on two factors" and describes only accuracy and evaluator stake, then appends the yellow stub: "Three: likelihood that your organization's candidate wins [fix writing]". Evaluator NEW ROW 7 discloses only "their payment partially depends on the accuracy of their endorsement... their payment also depends on your willingness to follow their judgment." No text in either tab describes the social-capital allocations paying the sponsor.
findings.why_it_matters: The canonical IRB constraint is that every downstream consequence told to evaluators must actually pay the sponsor, and Stage 2 must disclose all bonus components. As written, Stage 2 tells sponsors 'two factors' while a third is half-drafted, the Stage 2 comprehension check (ROW 7) only tests the two-factor scheme, and the planned social-capital telegraph (the study's core new DV) has no corresponding disclosure or payment rule anywhere. Fielding either stage as written makes the eventual telegraph language deceptive or the sponsor consent incomplete.
findings.proposed_fix: Finish the ROW 6 third-factor text, update the opening sentence to the true number of factors, extend the ROW 7 comprehension item, and add matching truthful language to the Evaluator tab (e.g., "Your end-of-study allocations about this organization and this sponsor will affect the sponsor's bonus") only once the Stage 2 payment rule actually implements it.
findings.verdict_notes: Every quoted piece of evidence exists exactly where claimed. tab_endorser.txt ROW 6 opens "Your earnings depend on two factors", enumerates only (1) accuracy and (2) evaluator stake, then ends with the yellow-highlighted stub "Three: likelihood that your organization's candidate wins [fix writing]" — an internal contradiction with no payment rule for the third factor. tab_endorser.txt ROW 7's comprehension item tests only the two-factor scheme. tab_evaluator.txt NEW ROW 7 discloses only "their payment partially depends on the accuracy of their endorsement... their payment also depends on your willingness to follow their judgment." Grep confirms zero mentions of the social-capital telegraph, slot allocations, or any third payment channel in either the Endorser or Evaluator tab; the telegraph appears only in meeting notes (tab_4_16_meeting.txt line 31) and archive tabs. This directly violates canonical hard flag 1 (telegraph truthfulness / full Stage 2 bonus disclosure), so critical severity is warranted. Minor context: the Evaluator NEW table also omits the 3-round structure and social-capital DV screens entirely (ROW 8: "you will evaluate two decisions"), which the finding's "no corresponding disclosure or payment rule anywhere" phrasing already covers.

findings.title: Outcome sequence and round structure unspecified: two decisions instead of three rounds, no pre-balancing, no cross-arm identity statement
findings.location: Evaluator tab (NEW) TABLE ROW 8, ROW 9 (CQ5), ROW 10
findings.evidence: ROW 8: "Today you will evaluate two decisions made by the same endorser." and "You will find out whether the endorser was right immediately after each wager." ROW 10: "Today you will evaluate one endorser and their two decisions." CQ5 correct answer: "The sum of both decisions". Nothing anywhere in the NEW table states how outcomes are determined, that the sequence contains at least one hit and one miss, or that sequences are identical across Man/Woman arms.
findings.why_it_matters: The primary model is delta_wager ~ prev_outcome * endorser_female with a round term; the canonical design is THREE rounds with a PRE-BALANCED outcome sequence identical across gender arms. With two decisions there is a single delta per person, and with outcome sequences unspecified (possibly real, endorsement-dependent outcomes), the focal prev_outcome x gender interaction is confounded by whatever outcome mix each arm happens to receive. A coauthor reading the doc cannot tell whether outcomes are scripted at all.
findings.proposed_fix: Update ROW 8/10 and CQ5 to three rounds (or add a bracketed note that two decisions is pilot-only, per unresolved comment "Just one endorser for the pilot"), and add: "[Outcome sequence is pre-assigned: each participant sees at least one correct and one incorrect outcome; sequences are counterbalanced and identical across the Man and Woman arms.]"
findings.verdict_notes: Core claim confirmed: the Evaluator NEW table specifies two decisions (ROW 8 line "Today you will evaluate two decisions made by the same endorser.", ROW 10 "Today you will evaluate one endorser and their two decisions.", CQ5 "The sum of both decisions") versus the canonical three rounds, and contains no statement of pre-balanced/counterbalanced outcome sequences or cross-arm (Man/Woman) identity anywhere; the cited unresolved comment "Just one endorser for the pilot" exists in doc_comments.txt (anchored to "Now, you will evaluate 2 endorser decisions."). Severity 'critical' is warranted since the primary model (round term, prev_outcome x gender) presumes three pre-balanced rounds. One evidence sentence needs correction: it is not true that "Nothing anywhere in the NEW table states how outcomes are determined" — ROW 7 states outcomes are determined by real candidate performance ("their candidate does indeed perform better/worse than the randomly chosen alternate participant"). That correction strengthens rather than weakens the finding: the doc affirmatively implies real, unscripted outcomes, directly contradicting the mandated pre-balanced sequence, not merely omitting it.
findings.corrected: Replace the evidence clause "Nothing anywhere in the NEW table states how outcomes are determined..." with: "The only outcome-determination language in the NEW table is ROW 7's 'their candidate does indeed perform better/worse than the randomly chosen alternate participant', which implies real, endorsement-dependent outcomes; nothing states that sequences are pre-assigned, contain at least one hit and one miss, or are identical across Man/Woman arms." All quotes and row locations (Evaluator NEW ROW 8, ROW 9 CQ5, ROW 10) are otherwise accurate.

findings.title: Slider pole orientation inconsistent: text anchors by left/right candidate, mockup anchors own-org on the LEFT, canonical spec anchors own-org on the RIGHT
findings.location: Endorser tab TABLE ROW 4 vs ROW 12 proposed mockup (kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz)
findings.evidence: ROW 4: "moving the slider toward 0 indicates you favor the candidate on the left, moving it toward 100 indicates you favor the candidate on the right". The proposed mockup labels the poles "Vertex candidate" (left, 0) and "Beacon candidate" (right, 100), i.e. own org at 0. The canonical panel decision relabels poles by org with own org anchored on the right.
findings.why_it_matters: The signed strength/direction coding (|v-50|*2 plus favoredSide) that feeds the evaluator display depends on a fixed, known pole convention. Three conventions currently coexist in the doc (generic left/right candidate, own-org-left mockup, own-org-right canonical). If screens are built from the mockup while analysis code assumes own-org-right, own-org endorsements get coded as rival endorsements, corrupting both the displayed stimuli and the endorsement-strength covariate.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one convention (canonical: own org on the right, pole labels by org name), update ROW 4's instruction text to describe org-anchored poles instead of "candidate on the left/right", and regenerate the mockup slider labels to match.
findings.verdict_notes: All evidence verified verbatim. Endorser tab ROW 4 (tab_endorser.txt) contains exactly the quoted instruction text anchoring poles by generic left/right candidate. The ROW 12 proposed mockup (images/Endorser__mxo6oc7vxrwz.png) labels the slider poles "Vertex candidate" (left, 0) and "Beacon candidate" (right, 100); ROW 4 establishes Vertex = the sponsor's own org, so the mockup anchors own-org at 0/left. The canonical brief mandates "relabel the poles by org (own org anchored on the right)". Three conflicting conventions therefore coexist as claimed, and the |v-50|*2 + favoredSide coding pipeline depends on a fixed pole convention, so the severity logic holds. Caveat (not a refutation): the proposed mockups in rows 12, 13, and 15 are byte-identical duplicates (156,962 bytes), which the brief flags as known duplicated placeholders, so the own-org-left orientation may stem from one placeholder image reused; the doc as it stands still shows the inconsistent convention.

findings.title: Org-level vs sponsor-level social-capital DVs are collinear by design and the doc neither contains the items nor acknowledges the confound
findings.location: Evaluator tab (NEW) — items absent (table ends at ROW 13); 4/16 Meeting tab lines "Do you want to keep seeing candidates from this organization / Do you want to keep seeing candidates from this sponsor?"
findings.evidence: The NEW Evaluator table contains no social-capital allocation items and no exit self-endorsement; the only trace is the 4/16 meeting note: "Repeated rounds (3 rounds) / Binary items (telegraph this to the sponsor as a bonus) - anyway to make this continuous? / Do you want to keep seeing candidates from this organization / Do you want to keep seeing candidates from this sponsor? / Exit interview (endorser's endorsement)".
findings.why_it_matters: Because the evaluator sees one sponsor from one org for all rounds, the org-level and sponsor-level allocations share identical exposure history — they cannot be dissociated, and any gender effect on the sponsor item will mechanically appear on the org item. This is known hard flag 3, and the doc currently handles it by omission: no items, no acknowledgment, no design feature (e.g., a second same-org sponsor, or explicit framing that the org item is a spillover measure) and no analysis note.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the two 0-10 slot-allocation items and the exit self-endorsement to the NEW table verbatim, plus a bracketed note: "[Org and sponsor allocations are collinear by design (one sponsor per org per participant); the org item is interpreted as reputational spillover, not an independent effect. Analyze separately, never as competing predictors.]"
findings.verdict_notes: All evidence checks out. (1) The NEW Evaluator table in tab_evaluator.txt really ends at "==== TABLE ROW 13 ====" (rows 11-13 are mockup-image rows only), and contains no 0-10 slot-allocation items, no org/sponsor "keep seeing" items, and no exit self-endorsement; rows 8 and 10 even still say "two decisions" rather than 3 rounds. (2) The 4/16 Meeting tab (lines 30-34) contains the quoted trace verbatim: "Repeated rounds (3 rounds) / Binary items (telegraph this to the sponsor as a bonus) – anyway to make this continuous? / Do you want to keep seeing candidates from this organization / Do you want to keep seeing candidates from this sponsor? / Exit interview (endorser's endorsement)" (doc uses an en dash, finding quoted a hyphen — immaterial). (3) Grep across all scratchpad files for "collinear|dissociat|spillover|confound" and "keep seeing|slot|social capital" shows the only mentions are in design_context.md itself and the meeting note — nothing in the Endorser tab, Evaluator tab (NEW or OLD), or the 24 doc comments acknowledges or handles the org-vs-sponsor collinearity. The problem follows directly from canonical hard flag 3 ("same sponsor = same org for all 3 rounds... collinear by design; cannot be dissociated") and audit asks 1 and 3. Severity "important" is defensible within the confounds lens (the pure absence of the items is a completeness issue; the confound-specific gap is the missing acknowledgment/analysis note).

findings.title: Evaluator-to-sponsor payment mapping under-specified, so the Stage 3 influence claim is only probabilistically true
findings.location: Endorser tab TABLE ROW 6; Evaluator tab (NEW) TABLE ROW 7
findings.evidence: Endorser ROW 6: "Your bonus earnings are based on one of your endorsements, selected at random" and "you'll earn the same proportion of the $3 as evaluators were willing to stake on your endorsement." Evaluator NEW ROW 7: "even if the endorser's judgment proves to be correct, if you do not wager part of your earnings on their decision, their payment will not be as high."
findings.why_it_matters: With N~100 sponsors, ~600 evaluators, multiple wagers per evaluator, and sponsor pay based on ONE randomly selected endorsement, an individual evaluator's wager affects the sponsor only if that endorsement-wager pair is drawn. The doc never defines which evaluator's wager (or which round's wager) feeds the $3 formula. As written, the Stage 3 statement overstates each evaluator's causal influence, which is both an IRB truthfulness risk and a demand-relevant inflation of the wager's perceived stakes; it could also differ in salience across arms if left to ad hoc implementation.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify the mapping in Endorser ROW 6 (e.g., "one endorsement AND one evaluator wager on it will be selected at random; your bonus equals $3 x that evaluator's wager percentage if the endorsement was correct") and soften Evaluator ROW 7 to the truthful form ("if your wager is selected, the sponsor's bonus is scaled by how much you wagered").
findings.verdict_notes: All quoted evidence verified verbatim at the claimed locations. Endorser tab ROW 6 contains both "Your bonus earnings are based on one of your endorsements, selected at random" and "you'll earn the same proportion of the $3 as evaluators were willing to stake on your endorsement" (note the plural "evaluators" against a single randomly selected endorsement — the ambiguity is right there in the sentence). Evaluator NEW tab ROW 7 contains "even if the endorser's judgment proves to be correct, if you do not wager part of your earnings on their decision, their payment will not be as high" stated deterministically. The core problem follows from the canonical brief: with N~100 sponsors and ~600 evaluators, multiple evaluators see the same sponsor and each makes multiple wagers (NEW tab ROW 8: "you will evaluate two decisions made by the same endorser"), yet nothing in either tab defines which evaluator's wager, or which decision's wager, feeds the $3 formula when the one random endorsement is drawn, nor whether multiple evaluators' wagers on the same endorsement are averaged or sampled. The Evaluator tab also never discloses the random-selection mechanism at all (only the Endorser tab does), so the evaluator-facing causal claim overstates each individual wager's influence — squarely the brief's hard flag #1 (TELEGRAPH TRUTHFULNESS / IRB: "anything evaluators are told about affecting the sponsor's pay must be true"). I attempted the refutation that the statement is true "in expectation," but that defense fails because the evaluator is never told selection is probabilistic, so the deterministic reading is the only one available to them. Severity "important" is appropriate; one could argue "critical" given the explicit IRB flag, but since the fix is a wording/specification change rather than a design change, "important" is defensible. Location, quotes, and logic all check out.

findings.title: Fielded-study wagers would be non-incentive-compatible if the comprehension-pretest framing in ROW 4 is retained
findings.location: Evaluator tab (NEW) TABLE ROW 4
findings.evidence: ROW 4: "The purpose of this study is to test people's comprehension of the following instructions we are going to be using for a future study. So please read them carefully, as we will be asking comprehension check questions at the end."
findings.why_it_matters: This row frames the entire NEW table as an instructions pretest, but nothing marks it as pretest-only. If a coauthor or implementer builds the fielded Stage 3 from this table, participants are explicitly told the wagers belong to "a future study", making the per-round wager DV hypothetical and destroying its incentive compatibility. Conversely, if this IS only the pretest, the doc contains no fielded version of the Stage 3 opening.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap ROW 4 in an implementation note: "[PRETEST WRAPPER ONLY - delete for the fielded study]" and add the fielded-study opening row (real-stakes framing) so the two versions cannot be conflated.
findings.verdict_notes: Quote is verbatim at tab_evaluator.txt line 17, NEW table ROW 4, unhighlighted and with no bracketed implementation note marking it pretest-only. No doc comment addresses it (doc_comments.txt has no match for pretest/future study/comprehension). The very next row (ROW 5) uses real-stakes wager language, so the "future study" wrapper directly contradicts the canonical Stage 3 design where the per-round wager on a $0.50 bank is a real incentive-compatible DV. The secondary claim also checks out: the only other Stage 3 opening is OLD table ROW 4 (lines 134-147), which uses the deprecated $2-bonus/"stake" scheme, so the doc has no fielded-study opening for the current design. Severity 'important' is appropriate.

findings.title: Org badge colors and counterbalancing unspecified; mockups render every org as the same yellow pill and the two tabs use different org names
findings.location: Endorser tab ROW 12 mockup (Vertex and Beacon badges both yellow); Evaluator tab ROWS 11-13 proposed mockups (Atlas badge, same yellow pill); doc text nowhere specifies badge colors
findings.evidence: In kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz both the "Vertex" and "Beacon" badges are identical yellow pills; in kix.vha7uuc4k2ve and kix.x95kfkt7nmdu the endorser and candidate both carry a yellow "Atlas" badge. No table text states the canonical org palette (Atlas violet #7C3AED, Vertex amber #B45309, Beacon teal #0F766E) or the constraint that badges must stay off the pink/blue gender palette, and nothing says org-name assignment is counterbalanced across participants.
findings.why_it_matters: Badge color is the one visual element that could accidentally land on the gender palette (a blue-ish or pink-ish org badge would contaminate the avatar-color manipulation). The doc currently leaves badge color to the implementer, and the Endorser tab (Vertex/Beacon) vs Evaluator tab (Atlas) mismatch obscures whether org identity is held constant, rotated, or counterbalanced across the sponsor-gender arms.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a bracketed stimulus note in both tabs: "[Org badges: Atlas violet #7C3AED, Vertex amber #B45309, Beacon teal #0F766E - deliberately off the gender palette (blue #2563EB/#3B82F6, pink #DB2777/#EC4899). Org names are placeholders, counterbalanced across participants and crossed with endorser gender.]"
findings.verdict_notes: Core claim confirmed: Endorser ROW 12 proposed mockup (kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz) renders Vertex and Beacon as identical yellow pills; Evaluator proposed mockups (kix.vha7uuc4k2ve, kix.x95kfkt7nmdu) render Atlas as the same yellow pill on both endorser and candidate cards; no doc text anywhere specifies the canonical badge palette (Atlas violet #7C3AED, Vertex amber #B45309, Beacon teal #0F766E) or the off-gender-palette constraint, and the Evaluator tab text never names any org (0 grep hits), so the Vertex/Beacon vs Atlas mismatch exists only across images. Two adjustments: (1) location - the two cited Evaluator images sit in TABLE ROWS 11 and 12, not 11-13 (ROW 13 holds kix.trax2nf87a9a, uncited); (2) the counterbalancing clause is an addition beyond the canonical brief, which only calls org names swappable placeholders and never mandates counterbalancing, so that part is a suggestion, not a doc-vs-brief deviation. Severity 'minor' is appropriate.
findings.corrected: Endorser tab ROW 12 proposed mockup [IMAGE:kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz] (Vertex and Beacon badges both identical yellow pills); Evaluator tab ROW 11 [IMAGE:kix.vha7uuc4k2ve] and ROW 12 [IMAGE:kix.x95kfkt7nmdu] (yellow Atlas pill on both endorser and candidate cards). No text in tab_endorser.txt, tab_evaluator.txt, or doc_comments.txt specifies badge colors, the off-gender-palette constraint, or org-name assignment; Evaluator tab body text contains no org names at all.

findings.title: Only the Man/blue endorser condition is mocked up; Woman/pink arm parity cannot be verified from the doc
findings.location: Evaluator tab (NEW) TABLE ROWS 11-13 - all six images (kix.is8axhdh3ngr, kix.vha7uuc4k2ve, kix.1ddd2y5mgo2u, kix.x95kfkt7nmdu, kix.trax2nf87a9a, kix.ybinacxhn5nc) show a man-silhouette endorser with blue ring and blue "Endorser" pill
findings.evidence: Every current and proposed Evaluator mockup shows the same man avatar, blue border ring, and blue pill; ROWS 12 and 13's "current" and "Proposed" images are byte-identical duplicates of ROW 11's (140761 and 148032 bytes respectively). No Woman/pink-styled card appears anywhere in either tab.
findings.why_it_matters: The entire manipulation is carried by avatar color styling, so visual parity (salience, contrast, badge-vs-ring color interaction, e.g., pink ring against the yellow Atlas badge) between arms is exactly what a design-doc reviewer needs to check - and currently cannot. The duplicated round-2/round-3 placeholders also hide whether later-round screens differ (jittered strength, outcome recap).
findings.proposed_fix: Add one Woman-condition proposed mockup per screen type (evaluation, outcome) alongside the Man versions, and replace the duplicated ROW 12/13 images with true round-2 screens showing the jittered strength value.
findings.verdict_notes: Core claim CONFIRMED: all six images in Evaluator NEW-table rows 11-13 (kix.is8axhdh3ngr, kix.vha7uuc4k2ve, kix.1ddd2y5mgo2u, kix.x95kfkt7nmdu, kix.trax2nf87a9a, kix.ybinacxhn5nc) were opened and every one shows the same man-silhouette endorser with a blue ring and blue "Endorser" pill (proposed versions add the yellow Atlas badge). Grep for woman/pink/female over tab_evaluator.txt returns no matches, and no pink-styled endorser card exists in any of the 20 images (the only woman silhouette anywhere is a gray CANDIDATE avatar in the Endorser-tab proposed mockup kix.mxo6oc7vxrwz, which is a different issue). Since the canonical brief says the manipulation is carried ONLY by avatar color styling (Man blue vs Woman pink), the inability to verify arm parity from the doc follows, and 'minor' severity is reasonable. However, one evidentiary detail is wrong: the finding claims ROWS 12 AND 13 duplicate ROW 11, but only ROW 13's pair is byte-identical to ROW 11's (140761 and 148032 bytes per images_manifest.json). ROW 12's images (151196 and 158463 bytes) are distinct and show a different screen type — the outcome/"Outcome of the last endorsement" screen — not duplicates. So the outcome screen IS mocked up; what the ROW 13 duplicates hide is only the round-2/later-round evaluation screen (jittered strength), and the proposed fix should be narrowed accordingly. Note also the design brief itself concedes "several are known to be duplicated placeholders", which supports treating the duplication part as known/minor rather than a discovery.
findings.corrected: Corrected evidence: Evaluator tab NEW table, ROWS 11-13. ROW 11 (current kix.is8axhdh3ngr / proposed kix.vha7uuc4k2ve) = evaluation screen; ROW 12 (kix.1ddd2y5mgo2u / kix.x95kfkt7nmdu) = outcome screen, distinct images (151196 / 158463 bytes); ROW 13 (kix.trax2nf87a9a / kix.ybinacxhn5nc) = byte-identical duplicates of ROW 11's pair (140761 / 148032 bytes). All six show only the Man/blue endorser; no Woman/pink mockup exists in either tab. Corrected claim: only ROW 13 is a duplicated placeholder (hiding the round-2 jittered-strength screen); the outcome screen is already mocked up in ROW 12.

findings.title: Stage 2 still describes the evaluator DV as 'stake'/'bet' on 'their own bonus', contradicting the wager/$0.50-bank scheme evaluators actually face
findings.location: Endorser tab TABLE ROW 5 and ROW 6 (unhighlighted text)
findings.evidence: ROW 5: "they will decide what percentage of their own bonus (0-100%) to stake on your endorsement being correct." ROW 6: "how much the evaluator was willing to stake on that endorsement decision" and "the more they bet, the larger your bonus." The Evaluator NEW table uses "wager" and "$0.50 bank" throughout (ROW 8).
findings.why_it_matters: The banned "stake" terminology survives unhighlighted in Stage 2, so the sponsor's mental model of the evaluator's decision (a share of 'their own bonus') mismatches the actual per-round $0.50-bank wager. Beyond convention, if Stage 2 screens ever quote or telegraph the evaluator mechanism, the description would be inaccurate; and stale unhighlighted text violates the yellow-means-changed convention, hiding that this passage still needs updating.
findings.proposed_fix: In ROWS 5-6 replace "stake"/"bet" with "wager" and describe the mechanism truthfully ("decide what percentage of a $0.50 bank per decision (0-100%) to wager"), highlighting the change in yellow.
findings.verdict_notes: All quotes exist verbatim (modulo en dash vs hyphen in "(0–100%)") at the claimed locations: Endorser tab ROW 5 and ROW 6 contain unhighlighted "stake"/"bet"/"their own bonus"/"their own earnings" language, while Evaluator NEW table ROW 8 uses the canonical "$0.50 bank"/"wager" scheme. The design brief explicitly bans "stake" and mandates the yellow-means-changed convention, so both the terminology violation and the stale-unhighlighted-text problem follow directly. Severity 'minor' is reasonable, though arguably 'important' since Stage 2's description of the evaluator mechanism ("percentage of their own bonus") is substantively inaccurate relative to the per-decision $0.50-bank wager, which touches the telegraph-truthfulness flag.

findings.title: Stale two-decision structure on Evaluator NEW table is entirely unhighlighted despite canonical three-round design
findings.location: Evaluator tab, NEW table, TABLE ROW 8, ROW 9 (CQ5), and ROW 10
findings.evidence: ROW 8: "Today you will evaluate two decisions made by the same endorser." and "Your total bonus is the sum of both decisions (up to $2.00 maximum)." ROW 9 CQ5: "5. How is your total bonus calculated? ... The sum of both decisions (correct)". ROW 10: "Today you will evaluate one endorser and their two decisions. Click the arrow to begin." None of these sit inside any [HL#ffff00] run.
findings.why_it_matters: The canonical design is three rounds (R1 -> outcome -> R2 -> outcome -> R3 -> outcome) with a new candidate pair each round. This is verbatim fielded-pilot text (the pilot had exactly two decisions), so under the yellow-equals-changed convention its lack of highlighting tells a coauthor the two-decision structure is settled and unchanged, when it is the single largest structural change in Stage 3. It also silently carries the wrong bonus cap ($2.00 instead of $3.00 for three $0.50 banks).
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite ROW 8 to "Today you will evaluate three decisions made by the same endorser." and "Your total bonus is the sum of all three decisions (up to $3.00 maximum).", ROW 10 to "...one endorser and their three decisions.", and CQ5's correct option to "The sum of all three decisions", then yellow-highlight every changed span.
findings.verdict_notes: Every quoted span exists exactly where claimed in the Evaluator NEW table (tab_evaluator.txt lines 38, 45, 72-75, 79), and none sits inside any [HL#ffff00] run (rows 8-10 contain zero highlight markers; highlights_inventory.txt has no entry containing "two decisions" or "both decisions"). The canonical brief specifies Stage 3 as three rounds with a $0.50 bank per decision, so the two-decision language and the $2.00 cap are stale pilot text that must change, and the yellow-equals-changed convention makes its unhighlighted state actively misleading. Severity 'critical' is justified: fielding as written contradicts the core three-round structure and understates the max bonus. The proposed fix's arithmetic is also correct (3 x $1.00 max = $3.00).

findings.title: Unhighlighted CQ2 keyed-correct answer contradicts the adjacent yellow-highlighted rival-org comparison text
findings.location: Evaluator tab, NEW table, TABLE ROW 9 (CQ2), contradicting highlighted text in TABLE ROW 6
findings.evidence: ROW 9 (unhighlighted): "2. Who is the endorsed candidate compared against to determine whether the prediction was correct? • A randomly selected candidate from the remaining pool (correct)". ROW 6 (highlighted): "...would score higher on the logical-reasoning test than another randomly selected candidate [HL#ffff00]from the other organization. [/HL]"
findings.why_it_matters: Under the redesign the comparison is the specific rival-org candidate in the pair, not a random draw from a pool. A participant who correctly absorbs the new highlighted instructions would fail this unrevised comprehension check and be screened out (screen-out is any wrong answer), which would invalidate fielding. Because the row carries no yellow, it masquerades as settled pilot text that needs no update.
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the keyed answer to something like "The candidate from the other organization in the same candidate set" (and adjust distractors), yellow-highlight the change, and simultaneously delete the stale "randomly selected" in ROW 6 (highlighting that deletion-adjacent rewrite too).
findings.verdict_notes: Evidence verified verbatim: Evaluator NEW table ROW 9 CQ2 keyed answer 'A randomly selected candidate from the remaining pool (correct)' is unhighlighted (highlights_inventory.txt lists only five Evaluator highlight runs, all in ROW 6), and ROW 6 was updated with '[HL#ffff00]from the other organization. [/HL]'. The stale-text claim holds and matches the canonical design (own-org vs rival-org pair) and audit ask #6. However, the screen-out mechanism is overstated, so severity should drop from critical to important: ROW 6's current text still says 'another RANDOMLY SELECTED candidate from the other organization', so the keyed answer is not contradicted on 'randomly selected', only on 'remaining pool' vs 'from the other organization'; and none of the three distractors mentions the other organization, so a participant who absorbed the new instructions would still pick the keyed answer as the only plausible option and pass. The fix (rewrite keyed answer + distractors to name the rival-org candidate, highlight the change, and reconcile ROW 6's retained 'randomly selected') is correct as proposed.
findings.corrected: Severity: important (not critical). Location and quotes are accurate as stated: tab_evaluator.txt NEW table, ROW 9 lines 56-57 vs ROW 6 line 28. Corrected why-it-matters: the unhighlighted CQ2 answer is stale relative to the redesign ('remaining pool' has no org framing and implies the old pooled-comparison design), violating the yellow-highlight convention and risking a coauthor treating it as settled text; but it would not systematically screen out participants, because 'randomly selected' still appears in the updated ROW 6 instructions and the keyed answer remains the only plausible choice among the distractors.

In tab_endorser.txt, TABLE ROW 4, the sentence "Based on the information you receive, your task is to predict which candidate, A or B, will perform better on a separate logical reasoning test." (line 18) and the full slider paragraph "...moving the slider toward 0 indicates you favor the candidate on the left, moving it toward 100 indicates you favor the candidate on the right, and placing it closer to 50 indicates you are unsure..." findings.title: Banned "stake"/"bet" terminology and old evaluator-DV description unhighlighted on Endorser tab while Evaluator tab uses "wager"
findings.location: Endorser tab, TABLE ROW 5 (immediately after the highlighted run at inventory line 4) and TABLE ROW 6

The Evaluator NEW table, by contrast, uses the mandated terms: ROW 5 "willing to wager part of your own compensation", ROW 8 "you start with a bank of $0.50".

Because ROW 5's stale sentence directly follows a yellow run describing what the evaluator will see, the unhighlighted continuation reads as reviewed-and-settled, and the two tabs now describe the same mechanism in incompatible language.

findings.title: Unhighlighted comprehension-pretest boilerplate opens the NEW Evaluator table as if it were settled study text
findings.location: Evaluator tab, NEW table, TABLE ROW 4
findings.evidence: "The purpose of this study is to test people’s comprehension of the following instructions we are going to be using for a future study. So please read them carefully, as we will be asking comprehension check questions at the end." No highlight, no [bracketed implementation note].
findings.why_it_matters: This is leftover framing from the March 2026 instructions pretest, not the canonical Stage 3, where evaluators actually wager real money across rounds (ROWS 5-8 describe real payouts). Presented unhighlighted and unbracketed inside the "current working version" table, it misleads a coauthor into thinking the fielded Stage 3 will tell participants the study is only a comprehension test of future instructions, which is false for the real study.
findings.proposed_fix: Either delete the row for the fielded design, or wrap it as an implementation note, e.g. "[Pretest-only screen, remove for fielded study: The purpose of this study is to test people's comprehension...]", and yellow-highlight it if it is retained in modified form.
findings.verdict_notes: The quoted sentence exists verbatim and exactly where claimed: Evaluator tab, NEW table, TABLE ROW 4 (tab_evaluator.txt lines 16-17): "The purpose of this study is to test people's comprehension of the following instructions we are going to be using for a future study. So please read them carefully, as we will be asking comprehension check questions at the end." It carries no [HL] highlight run (no match for "comprehension" anywhere in highlights_inventory.txt) and no [bracketed implementation note], and no unresolved doc comment addresses it (no match for comprehension/pretest/"future study" in doc_comments.txt). The problem follows from the canonical brief: Stage 3 evaluators actually wager a $0.50 bank per decision with real payouts, which the same table asserts in ROW 5 ("wager part of your own compensation"), ROW 7, and ROW 8 ("If the endorser was right, then you get your $0.50 plus whatever you wagered"), directly contradicting a purpose statement that the study is only a comprehension test of future instructions. The framing matches the March 2026 instructions-pretest survey (SV_bjFLJsMzBFTpJvo), and the OLD (archive) table has no such row, so this is text new relative to the fielded pilot that is also unhighlighted, a second violation of the yellow=new/changed convention. Severity 'important' is apt: it misleads a coauthor about what fielded participants will be told but is a one-row fix. One minor evidence nuance: of ROWS 5-8 cited as describing real payouts, ROW 6 is setup description; the real-payout language is in ROWS 5, 7, and 8 — this does not weaken the claim.

findings.title: Inconsistent highlight granularity across tabs plus trailing whitespace/paragraph marks inside runs; all runs are yellow

findings.evidence: Endorser runs are whole paragraphs ending in a highlighted newline, e.g. "'You have been assigned to represent [ORGANIZATION 1: Vertex].\n'" (inventory line 1), while the Evaluator tab mixes a whole-paragraph run (line 8) with mid-sentence fragments: "'from their own organization'" (lines 9, 11) and "'from the other organization. \n'" (line 10, capturing the trailing period, space, and paragraph mark); inventory line 4 also ends in a stray trailing space: "'...and your slider position. [/HL]Based on that information...' in tab_endorser.txt line 24), so fragmented granularity exists within the Endorser tab too, not only on the Evaluator tab. Severity 'minor' stands.

gaps.title: CRITICAL - Scripted-stimuli fixes and truthfulness fixes are jointly unsatisfiable; the yoking/deception architecture is undecided and undocumented
gaps.detail: Evaluator NEW ROW 5 promises: "we will be showing you information about another participant's real decisions," and ROW 7 telegraphs real pay consequences ("their payment also depends on your willingness to follow their judgment"). But the confounds lens's proposed fix mandates the opposite: "[The displayed endorsement stream (direction and strength) is scripted and identical across Man/Woman arms; endorser gender is randomly assigned independent of endorsement content.]" The canonical jitter (later rounds display R1 confidence +/- 5-12 points) already means the displayed strength is NOT the endorser's real second/third decision, and random gender-avatar assignment means the shown gender need not be the real endorser's gender. No lens flagged that these fixes, if applied together, make ROW 5 false and the ROW 7 sponsor-pay telegraph untruthful (IRB hard flag 1), in a lab context that avoids deception. Three resolutions exist and the doc must pick one: (a) truthful yoking - sample real endorsers by gender and strength cell, show their actual decisions; internal-validity cost: endorsement content is no longer identical across gender arms, partially undoing the confounds fix; (b) scripted display with a matched real sponsor paid from the wagers; requires deception disclosure/debrief and likely conflicts with lab policy; (c) drop the "real decisions" claim and the sponsor-pay telegraph; cost: the social-capital telegraph (the core new DV mechanism) loses its truth grounding. This is the first question a coauthor will ask ("whose decisions are these actually?") and neither the doc nor any of the 6 lenses answers it.

gaps.title: CRITICAL - The panel's own proposed rewrites straddle both sides of the free-choice vs must-endorse fork; the fixes do not converge on one design
gaps.detail: The stage2 "Core task definition" fix uses must-endorse language ("decide how strongly to endorse [ORGANIZATION 1: Vertex]'s candidate, the candidate you represent"), while the stage2 "Slider description" fix uses free-choice language ("moving toward 0 means you favor the other organization's candidate"). The June-2 fixes ("The candidate they endorsed is always from the endorser's own organization") are truthful ONLY under must-endorse, or under free choice plus an own-org-favoring selection filter - and that filter is itself a confound nobody named: only sliders >50 would ever be shown, truncating the strength distribution and starving the weak-endorsement cells. Conversely, under free choice, Evaluator ROW 6's final paragraph ("You will also see whether the candidate they endorsed was from the endorser's own organization or from another organization") is the TRUTHFUL version, so the June-2 'critical' fix would be the wrong edit; the triage claim for AAAB8qTe4lg that the paragraph is wrong "whichever way that fork resolves" is incorrect for the free-choice branch. Additional un-flagged consequences of each branch: under free choice, an evaluator wagering on "the endorser being correct" when the endorser favored the rival is betting AGAINST the sponsor's own org, contaminating the slot-allocation DV's interpretation; under must-endorse, the retained bipolar 0-100 slider's lower half is incoherent and ROW 6's rule "if you placed your slider on the 50 mark, you cannot earn a bonus" penalizes honest uncertainty about a forced endorsement. The meeting needs a one-page decision matrix; every Stage 2 text fix, the June-2 fix, the comparison-standard fix, and the selection-rule note are all conditional on this single choice.

gaps.title: IMPORTANT - The panel gave two mutually inconsistent completions of the third bonus factor, and the 4/16 notes suggest a third reading; which mechanism factor three IS remains an undecided design question
gaps.detail: The stage2 lens completes the ROW 6 stub ("Three: likelihood that your organization's candidate wins [fix writing]") as the slot-allocation telegraph ("the evaluator allocates future review slots... each slot allocated adds $X to your bonus"). The highlights lens completes the SAME stub differently: "depends on how likely the evaluator believes your organization's candidate is to win" (i.e., evaluator wager direction/level). The stub's literal wording, plus the 4/16 note "Incentivized to pick performers from your organization," supports a third reading: the sponsor is paid when their own org's candidate wins, regardless of endorsement - the advocacy-stake mechanism that makes the sponsorship tension real. These three mechanisms have different incentive properties: (i) slot telegraph = social-capital return; (ii) evaluator-belief = pays for persuasion/extremity; (iii) own-org-win = advocacy stake. Both (ii) and (iii) directly conflict with ROW 10's instruction to "honestly indicate which candidate you believe will perform better" whenever the rival is objectively stronger - which may be the intended sponsorship conflict, but only if chosen deliberately and disclosed. Whichever is chosen determines the CQ rewrite, the Stage 3 telegraph text, and the IRB truthfulness audit. If a coauthor applies both lenses' fixes as written, the doc ends up with two contradictory factor-three sentences.

The forward-looking framing is false unless the allocation has a real referent - e.g., it truthfully determines the candidate-set composition shown to a future evaluator, or it is reframed as a recommendation with only the sponsor-bonus consequence. This is the same IRB hard flag 1 (telegraph truthfulness) the panel applied to sponsor pay, but nobody applied it to the DV item itself. The 4/16 phrasing ("Do you want to keep seeing candidates from this organization") has the identical problem. The row that gets added needs a bracketed note stating the item's actual real-world consequence.

gaps.title: IMPORTANT - Whether evaluators see the candidates' performance profiles is never stated; the 4/16 decision that they know 'only the confidence' was silently dropped
gaps.detail: 4/16 Meeting tab: "The evaluator considers how much to endorse the sponsors candidate (only knowing the confidence of Wharton)" - i.e., evaluators are blind to the percentile profiles. Evaluator NEW ROW 6 tells evaluators that ENDORSERS "were provided information about candidates' performance on the knowledge quiz and word-search puzzle" but never says whether the evaluator will or will not see that information; the mockups imply blindness (ID + org badge + confidence only) but no instruction or bracketed note records it. This is DV-defining: if evaluators saw the profiles, the wager measures their own forecast of candidate quality rather than trust in the endorser, and the gender effect would be diluted by an information channel that bypasses the endorser. Add one participant-facing sentence ("You will not see the candidates' performance information - only the endorser's decision") plus an implementation note.

gaps.title: IMPORTANT - Ceiling/floor censoring of the wager scale can mimic the 'muted updating' hypothesis; no lens covered this DV-confound
gaps.detail: The analysis DV is signed delta_wager on a 0-100% scale. If the gender arm shifts Round 1 wager LEVELS (the plausible baseline effect), the two arms sit at different distances from the bounds: an arm with lower R1 wagers has less room to move down after a miss and more room up after a hit, so between-arm differences in deltas can be produced by scale compression alone - and 'muted updating for women' is exactly the pattern bound-censoring generates from a lower baseline. The strong-strength tercile compounds this by pushing wagers toward the 100% ceiling. Nothing in the doc, the canonical brief's model (delta_wager ~ prev_outcome * endorser_female + ...), or any panel fix addresses it. Add an analysis note: check bound pileup in the pilot data, and pre-specify a censoring-aware model (e.g., tobit) or a baseline-wager control/robustness check so the focal interaction is not a compression artifact.

gaps.title: IMPORTANT - The 3-round condition structure is an undecided design, not a documentation gap: the old 8-cell design does not extend to three rounds
gaps.detail: The panel's implementation-notes finding treats "condition structure" as unrecorded documentation, and its proposed note stops at "outcome sequence pre-balanced >=1 hit >=1 miss, identical across arms." But with three rounds the between-subject factor {correct,incorrect} no longer exists: there are six sequences satisfying >=1 hit and >=1 miss (HHM, HMH, MHH, HMM, MHM, MMH), and the design must decide which are used, whether sequence is a randomized factor or counterbalanced nuisance, and how {strong,weak} maps onto tercile assignment across three jittered displays. The resulting cell count drives the power question the panel raised for the slot-allocation DV (>~403/cell) - you cannot write the N or the power note until the cell structure exists. This is a decision for the next meeting, and no row, note, or panel fix currently proposes the actual structure.

gaps.title: IMPORTANT - Stage 2's basic flow parameters are missing: number of candidate sets per sponsor, set composition, and supply feasibility for Stage 3 cells
gaps.detail: Endorser ROW 4 says only "you will act as an endorser. Your role is to evaluate a series of candidate sets" - the number of endorsement decisions per sponsor is stated nowhere in the tab (the four mockup rows are examples, not a count). ROW 5's "a subset of your endorsements will be shown to an evaluator" similarly leaves the supply side unspecified. This blocks three things coauthors will ask about: (1) whether N~100 sponsors x k sets can populate every Stage 3 cell, especially weak own-org endorsements under a free-choice resolution where most sponsors may slide strongly own-org (the advocacy incentive pushes them there); (2) whether each evaluator's three rounds can come from one sponsor with a pre-balanced hit/miss sequence drawn from real outcomes; (3) the stimulus-set design itself (how many dominant vs uncertain vs rival-better profiles, in what order). Add k, the profile composition, and a feasibility note to the Endorser tab.

The redesign's answer is that the slot-allocation DVs are consequential (they truthfully pay the sponsor), making them resistant to cheap socially desirable responding - but no doc text connects the incentive-compatible DV to that coauthor concern. Add one bracketed rationale note on the social-capital DV rows so the motivation survives; otherwise the same objection will be re-raised at the next meeting as if unaddressed.

gaps.title: MINOR - Three triage entries re-inject stale or fork-dependent design claims and should be corrected before anyone pastes them into the doc
gaps.detail: (1) AAABqogo0ic describes the current outcome rule as "endorsed candidate beats a randomly selected rival-org candidate," restating exactly the random-draw comparison standard that two critical findings order replaced with the paired same-set rival. (2) AAABtL3bCKM is closed on the ground that "endorsement strength is now an experimentally assigned factor," which presumes the scripted-stimuli resolution of the truthfulness fork (Gap 1) that is in fact unresolved; if the lab chooses truthful yoked sampling, oversampling extreme endorsers becomes live again rather than stale. (3) AAAB8qTe4lg's note "whichever way that fork resolves, this evaluator paragraph as written is wrong" is false for the free-choice branch, where the own-vs-other-org sentence is the truthful instruction (see Gap 2). None of these change the verdicts, but the action texts are what gets executed, so they should agree with the fixes.

critic.overall: The six lenses did thorough row-level work: every stale-text, highlight, image, and telegraph problem I checked against tab_endorser.txt and tab_evaluator.txt is real and correctly located, and I found no false positives in the row citations. What the panel missed is architectural. First, its fixes are not mutually consistent: the internal-validity fixes demand scripted, gender-independent, jittered endorsement streams while the truthfulness fixes demand that Evaluator ROW 5's "another participant's real decisions" and the sponsor-pay telegraph stay literally true - these cannot both hold, and the yoking/deception architecture that reconciles them is undecided (Gap 1). Second, the panel's own proposed rewrites straddle the free-choice vs must-endorse fork (must-endorse task language, free-choice slider language, June-2 fixes that are only truthful under must-endorse or a strength-truncating selection filter), so applying all fixes as written produces a self-contradictory doc; one design must be chosen first and everything re-derived from it (Gap 2). Third, analysis-critical elements no lens covered: the mandated manipulation check does not exist as an item anywhere (Gap 3), delta_wager is vulnerable to bound-censoring that can mimic the focal muted-updating prediction (Gap 7), and the 3-round condition structure is an unmade design decision, not missing documentation (Gap 8). Fourth, two 4/16 decisions were silently dropped beyond what the panel caught: evaluators knowing "only the confidence" (evaluator blindness to performance profiles, DV-defining) and the truth-grounding of the forward-looking slot-allocation items. Recommended meeting agenda order: resolve the fork (Gap 2), then the truthfulness architecture (Gap 1), then factor three (Gap 4); every other fix in the panel's list is conditional on those three choices.
